data.reasoning: The package contains standard AUR packaging for a .NET application. The PKGBUILD downloads source from the official GitHub repository with a pinned SHA256 checksum, uses standard dotnet publish for building, and installs binaries with appropriate permissions. No .install hooks, patches, or suspicious scripts are present. All successfully reviewed files contain only standard metadata, licensing, and configuration. The 'inconclusive' verdict from qwen was caused by API errors (HTTP 400) when processing .gitignore and LICENSE files, not by security concerns. The deepseek model successfully reviewed all files and found no issues.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement stems from infrastructure failures in the qwen model, which encountered HTTP 400 errors when attempting to audit .gitignore and LICENSE files. This caused those files to be marked inconclusive, triggering an overall inconclusive verdict. The deepseek model successfully reviewed all files without errors and correctly identified the package as safe. The openrouter report is advisory-only and does not count toward the verdict.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to review .gitignore and LICENSE due to API errors (HTTP 400 BadRequestError)
learnings: API errors during file review should not cause the entire package to be marked inconclusive when other files are successfully reviewed and found safe
The audit tool should distinguish between 'file could not be reviewed due to tool error' and 'file reviewed and found suspicious'
When multiple models review the same package, infrastructure failures in one model should not override successful reviews from other models
Consider implementing retry logic or fallback models when API errors occur during file review
